Krampusnacht Fiery Sausages with Peppers and Onions

Served at: Krampusnacht

Serves 4-6Prep 20 minCook 40 min

Krampusnacht, observed on the eve of St. Nicholas Day, is a time for hearty, warming fare to ward off the chill of December and perhaps the mischievous spirit of Krampus himself. These fiery sausages, simmered with sweet peppers and onions, offer a comforting and robust meal perfect for a cold winter's night, bringing warmth and flavor to your festive table.

Ingredients

  • 1.5 pounds (680 g) spicy Italian sausages (or other robust spicy pork sausages)
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) olive oil
  • 2 large bell peppers, any color (e.g., 1 red, 1 green), cored and sliced into strips
  • 1 large yellow onion, halved and sliced
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 teaspoon (5 ml) smoked paprika
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 ml) red pepper flakes (adjust to taste for heat)
  • 1 (14.5 ounce / 411 g) can diced tomatoes, undrained
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) chicken or beef broth
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

Method

  1. Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
  2. Add the sausages to the hot skillet and brown them on all sides, about 8-10 minutes. Remove sausages from the skillet and set aside, leaving rendered fat in the pan.
  3. Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced bell peppers and onion to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
  4. Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and red pepper flakes to the vegetables. Cook for 1 minute more, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
  5. Return the browned sausages to the skillet. Pour in the diced tomatoes (with their juice) and chicken or beef broth.
  6. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until sausages are cooked through and flavors have melded.
  7. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
  8. Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

Tips

  • For an even deeper flavor, use a good quality dark beer instead of broth.
  • Serve these sausages with crusty bread, creamy polenta, or roasted potatoes to soak up the delicious sauce.
  • The dish can be made ahead and reheated; the flavors often improve overnight.
